title: From Bachchan to Kher, Bollywood's Veterans Prove Fitness Has No Age Limit
excerpt: At 83, Amitabh Bachchan preaches caring for the body; at 88, Dharmendra mixes gym work with physiotherapy; at 70, Anupam Kher lifts heavy — Bollywood's senior stars are making strength after 70 look normal.
body:
• Amitabh Bachchan (83), Dharmendra (88), Anupam Kher (70) and Anil Kapoor are setting a new public standard for fitness past 70 in India.
  • Dharmendra combines gym workouts with physiotherapy; Kher posts weighted pull-downs and declared, "You can be a #PosterBoy even at seventy."
  • Milind Soman calls Bachchan "the fittest person that I know in India," crediting mental resilience as much as physical discipline.
  • Physiotherapists say the mix of strength work and rehab exercises these veterans model is exactly what doctors prescribe for healthy aging.

The video arrived without fanfare: Dharmendra, seated in a gym at 88, flexing toned thigh muscles for his Instagram followers. "Friends, I have started exercise and physiotherapy," the veteran actor said. "It's going well, I'm feeling great." Months later, Anupam Kher posted himself doing weighted pull-downs at 70. And Amitabh Bachchan, now 83, wrote on his blog that caring for the body is "prime at this age." A generation of Bollywood's biggest names is collectively rewriting the script on what growing old looks like.

Context & Background

The moments keep coming. In April 2025, Dharmendra shared an Instagram video from the gym showing well-toned leg muscles, telling fans he had folded both exercise and physiotherapy into his daily routine, according to Bollywood Hungama. Seated among the weights, the 88-year-old radiated energy, clearly pleased with his progress.

"Friends, I have started exercise and physiotherapy. It's going well, I'm feeling great. I hope you must be very happy to see me. Look at my thighs and muscles."

— Dharmendra, in an Instagram video

Anupam Kher has made gym posts something of a ritual. In November 2025, the 70-year-old actor shared snapshots of a gym session showing a toned physique, with a message of resilience: "The one who falls and gets up is stronger than the one who never tried." A month earlier he had posted a photo of his muscular back during a weighted pull-down, writing, "You can be a #PosterBoy even at seventy!!! Because you never know how strong you are until being strong is your only choice," Bollywood Hungama reported.

Anil Kapoor, now in his late 60s, remains the poster child of the cohort: running, cycling, planks, jump rope and weight lifting, plus a diet regime he credits for a physique that fans say has barely changed since his debut days. And at the top of the age ladder sits Amitabh Bachchan, who turned 83 this year and continues to host television, shoot films and write a near-daily blog. In a recent post he reflected that "work on the body is prime at this age," and that "work... work to get a living – work on your body – whatever, but work."

Impact & Analysis

What makes this more than celebrity vanity is the specific kind of fitness on display. The veterans are not just posting glamour shots; they are modeling the two things geriatric medicine actually recommends: resistance training to preserve muscle mass and bone density, and rehabilitative work like physiotherapy to manage pain and mobility. In an interview with HT Lifestyle cited by Bollywood Hungama, Dr. Varun Gupta noted that physiotherapy aids pain management, injury prevention and rehabilitation, better mobility and management of chronic conditions — precisely the toolkit Dharmendra now advertises to millions of followers.

"At the age of 80 plus, he is still enjoying life to the full. Whatever he wants, he is doing. Amitabh Bachchan is an amazing man, and he is the fittest person that I know in India."

— Milind Soman, fitness evangelist, to ANI

Soman, the supermodel-turned-fitness evangelist who founded the Pinkathon women's running movement, told ANI that true fitness goes beyond physical strength. He praised Bachchan for handling the stress and pressure of stardom and continuing to work actively on his own terms after crossing 80. The message lands in a country whose population is aging fast, where conversations about elder health still too often begin and end with medication.

Diaspora Angle

For Indians abroad, these posts travel further than any health-ministry campaign. NRIs watching parents age from thousands of miles away get a ready-made conversation starter — and a cultural counterweight to the idea that slowing down after 60 is inevitable. A Dharmendra gym video can do what nagging cannot: make strength training at 75 look normal, even aspirational.

What's Next

The trend shows no sign of slowing. Bachchan is slated to return for the sequel to the blockbuster Kalki 2898 AD, Kher keeps posting from the gym, and Soman's Pinkathon — which began with women walking 3 km and now includes 100 km ultradistances — is expanding from major metros into Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities, according to ANI. The bar for aging in public has moved, and the audience is watching.
